new_text: No match in which more than eleven players a side take part can be regarded as First-class, and in any case no side should field with more than eleven players.
In First-class matches in the United Kingdom the fielding side may demand a new ball after 65 (6 ball) overs have been bowled with the old one.

The normal rolling before the start of each day’s play shall take place not earlier than half an hour before the start of play, but the captain of the batting side may delay such rolling until 10 minutes before the start of play should he so desire.
(For the purpose of this rule a rest day counts as a day).
If flags or posts are used to mark a boundary, the real or imaginary line joining such points shall be regarded as the boundary, which should be marked by a white line if possible.
For the purpose of this and other Laws, the term “dress” includes the equipment and clothing of players and umpires as normally worn.
I.—The umpire shall regard the deliberate kicking or “kneeing” of the ball by the striker as unfair, and shall immediately call ”Dead Ball” in accordance with Law 25: no runs shall be allowed.
Any player may use his hand or arm to put the wicket down or, even should tbe bails be previously off, may pull up a stump, provided always that the ball is held in the hand or hands so used.
The striker is out “Bowled” under this Law when the ball is deflected on to his wicket off his person, even though a decision against him might be justified under Law 39 L.B.W.
A batsman may not attempt to hit the ball twice, if in so doing he baulks the wicket-keeper or any fieldsman attempting to make a catch.
